doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Getting into the Army band through Gil Rodin and Ray Bauduc
summary: His father arranged for Gil Rodin to request him for the Army band at Vallejo; the band played parades and dances.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And you joined the service, was it around ‘44 or ‘43?
Was it at that time, when you were going in the service, was it a question of I’m going overseas?

Well it’s funny I don’t know, in those days people, I don’t know, they weren’t as sensitive about it, maybe it’s since the Vietnam thing. Like if you could work deals, you know, nobody put you down. If you had connections where you could stay in the country for the duration or whatever, I mean it was fine, go do it. And my dad knew Gil Rodin, you are familiar with him? And he was up in Vallejo with Ray Bauduc, they were both in the same group up there. And I don’t know how my dad knew that, but he contacted Gil and told him I was going to be drafted, and if he could work something out that I could go up and join their band. And of course the Army bands were always looking for guys. And I think it was a legitimate thing, I mean you just couldn’t pull somebody that just © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

happened to come to the base, you know, oh, there’s a piano player. I mean you had to get them from someplace. So Gil said he’d see what he could do to get me up there. Because they did need a piano player.
Well quite a few of the people I’ve talked to had positive musical experiences in the military.

Yeah. Well they were considered important you know, morale and all that stuff. We played parades, we played the dances and the officers clubs, we were working almost every day. So yeah I think they thought it was important.
